incidents.title: The Snowing of Bar-Khel
incidents.summary: After orbital bombardment, Skymourn appeared above Bar-Khel. Within one week, the remaining citizens had frozen or entered exile; the snow did not melt.

militaryInterpretation: A post-battle psychological weapon that turns grief into persistent climate collapse. The documented combat profile names Thermal Ripple Burst, Sadness-Stasis Veil, and Melancholy Drift.

civicResponse.fieldEvidence: Extreme temperature divergence and persistent snowfall are documented around the Bar-Khel incident.
civicResponse.suspectedPropaganda: Claims that it sings the names of the dead are explicitly presented as unverified testimony.
civicResponse.archiveInterpretation: Treat grief-correlated thermal events as a detection signal, not proof of intent or range.

incidents.title: Fallenstar Prime
incidents.summary: The corrected war ledger places the first Blood Rings at Fallenstar Prime in Year 3, establishing the structure as a standard of conquest.

militaryInterpretation: Blood Rings are functional military ecology, not decoration. Documented roles include territorial marking, orbital shackling, demoralization, massacre scoring, and possible fortress or macro-defense functions.

civicResponse.fieldEvidence: Ground observers describe a red wound across the sky; orbital views reveal clot-veins, spin-striations, sealed fractures, ash plumes, and stabilization ribs.
civicResponse.suspectedPropaganda: The structure itself is a Drakken propaganda weapon. Any official reassurance must be evaluated separately from physical evidence.
civicResponse.archiveInterpretation: Treat the ring as active infrastructure until proven inert. The supplied source does not define a safe approach distance.
